subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (PII handling, retention, audit logs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Tanaka <sam.tanaka@noventa.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (PII handling, retention, audit logs)

Hi Sam 

Thanks again for taking the time to meet today. Below is a quick recap of what we heard, the success criteria you outlined, and proposed next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points
- PII in user prompts: need strong controls to prevent persistent storage of raw PII in hosted endpoints.
- Retention policy: must be able to set retention windows per-customer (90 days default; some customers require 30 days or less).
- Audit logging: need an immutable, per-request audit trail (who, when, prompt/response hashes, metadata) for compliance and troubleshooting.
- Redaction: automated redaction capability for defined PII types and a manual redaction workflow for edge cases.
- Encryption & key management: integration with customer KMS/HSM required for certain accounts.

Current stack you shared
- API layer: Noventa uses a mix of internal APIs + 3rd-party vendor LLMs today.
- Observability: Splunk for logs; S3 for long-term artifacts.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 in progress for several products; some customers are HIPAA-bound.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
1) Hosted or dedicated deployment that guarantees configurable retention (per-tenant) and ability to opt-out of storing request/response payloads.
2) Transparent, queryable audit logs with export capability (CSV/JSON) for 90-day retention and ability to shorten to 30/7 days per customer.
3) Support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest; TLS for in-flight.
4) Clear documentation and evidence (SOC2 summary, architecture diagrams) that we can present to Noventa security.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Retention policies: hosted API supports configurable retention windows and a 'no-logs' flag for sensitive routes. Dedicated/Private gives full control and per-tenant retention enforcement.
- Redaction & filtering: built-in configurable PII redaction pipeline (regex + model-based detectors) and manual redaction tooling.
- Audit logs: request/response metadata, hashes of content, user IDs, timestamps; signed export capabilities.
- KMS integrations: AWS KMS & customer-supplied HSM integrations in Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or optional BYOK for enterprise.

Attachments I’m sharing
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (one-pager summary of SOC2 scope and controls)
- redwood-retention-config-sample.yaml (example retention config you can apply per-tenant)
- nda-redwood-noventa-draft.docx (proposed mutual NDA if helpful)

Suggested next steps
1) Sam/Noventa: confirm the list of endpoints that must be "no-logs" or require shorter retention.
2) I’ll loop in our Security/Privacy lead (Dev) and Solutions (Rishi) for a technical Q&A next week to walk through config and KMS options.
3) If helpful, we can sign the NDA and share the SOC2 artifacts and a redacted SOC2 report under an NDA.
4) Proposed times for Technical Q&A: Tue 7/21 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 7/22 9:00–10:00 PT — which works for you?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once you confirm the time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Tanaka <sam.tanaka@noventa.ai>

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (PII handling, retention, audit logs)

Thanks Marissa — really appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Per-tenant retention: Yes, we need the ability to set retention per-tenant and also to mark certain customers as "no-logs" entirely for regulatory reasons. Can Redwood support an endpoint-level "no-logs" flag that bypasses storage?
- Redaction: model-based redaction sounds promising. Will that run inline (before storing) or post-hoc? Our preference is pre-storage redaction for obvious PII (SSNs, credit cards) and a manual review path for ambiguous cases.
- KMS/HSM: we need to confirm that keys can be customer-managed and that Redwood supports AWS KMS + in-prem HSM for Dedicated deployments.
- Audit logs: do you provide immutability guarantees (append-only, signed logs) or should we plan to ship logs into our Splunk/S3 pipeline for long-term retention?

Also: could you send over the SOC2 summary and any compliance questionnaire (we’ll have Infosec run through it)? I can also share our vendor security questionnaire — I’ll attach it to my next email.

Wed 7/22 9:00–10:00 PT works for a technical Q&A for me.

—Sam
Sam Tanaka
Head of Platform Security | Noventa AI
sam.tanaka@noventa.ai | +1 (617) 555-0910

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (PII handling, retention, audit logs)

Great — thanks for the quick reply, Sam. Answering your questions inline and adding next steps.

- Endpoint-level "no-logs" flag: Yes. Hosted API exposes a per-route flag that prevents request/response payloads from being persisted (we still log metadata for billing/ratelimit purposes unless "anonymize-metadata" is enabled). Dedicated/Private gives you the option to enforce true no-logs at the infra level.

- Redaction timing: Our standard offering runs PII detectors inline before persistence. The flow is: detect → mask/redact → store hashed artifact (if configured) + metadata. For ambiguous cases we surface the item to a queue for manual review; that queue can be configured to write to an internal ticketing system or S3 for auditors.

- KMS/HSM: Supported. Hosted: envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, BYOK via AWS KMS for enterprise accounts. Dedicated/Private: full customer-supplied KMS or HSM options and on-prem key injection where required.

- Audit log immutability: We provide append-only audit logs with signing and export capabilities. For long-term retention we recommend shipping to your Splunk/S3 pipeline — Redwood can push signed daily envelopes into your S3 bucket or you can pull via the secure export API.

Attachments I’ve included (again): redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-retention-config-sample.yaml, nda-redwood-noventa-draft.docx. If you prefer, we can gate the SOC2 report behind the NDA; otherwise the summary is fine to share publicly.

Next steps
1) I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 7/22 9–10 PT for the technical Q&A with Dev and Rishi.
2) If you can, send your vendor security questionnaire prior to the call so we can prepare answers; I’ll also ask our Security team to prioritize responses.
3) If NDA is helpful, we can get it signed this week — I’ve attached a draft.

Looping in Dev and Rishi to coordinate technical details and the call.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
